response.sql: WITH ev AS (SELECT e.event_id, e.type, AVG(b.spent * 1.0 / NULLIF(b.amount, 0)) AS event_rate FROM budget b JOIN event e ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event GROUP BY e.event_id, e.type), t AS (SELECT type, AVG(event_rate) AS avg_rate FROM ev GROUP BY type) SELECT type, avg_rate, avg_rate / (SELECT AVG(avg_rate) FROM t) AS ratio_to_mean FROM t;

assumptions.assumption: Budget lines with amount = 0 have an undefined rate (division by zero) and are treated as missing, so they are ignored in the averages. Lines with NULL spent or amount are also ignored. Lines with spent = 0 and a nonzero amount count as rate 0.
The simple mean of the per-type averages is an unweighted mean over types that have a non-null average rate. An event with a NULL type, if any exist, forms its own group and is included.
